1. **Representative Fraction (RF):**
   $$\text{Speed} = 50\text{ km/hr} \implies \text{Distance covered in } 1 \text{ hour} = 50\text{ km}$$
   $$\text{Scale length for } 1\text{ km} = 3\text{ cm}$$
   $$\text{RF} = \frac{\text{Length of drawing}}{\text{Actual length}} = \frac{3\text{ cm}}{1 \times 10^5\text{ cm}} = \frac{3}{100000}$$

2. **Length of Scale:**
   $$\text{Max length} = 6\text{ km} \implies \text{Length of line} = 6 \times 3\text{ cm} = 18\text{ cm}$.

3. **Construction Steps:**
   - Draw a line $18\text{ cm}$ long and divide it into $6$ equal parts (each representing $1\text{ km}$). Subdivide the first part into $10$ equal divisions ($0.1\text{ km}$ or $100\text{ m}$). 
   - Draw a vertical ladder of height $5\text{ cm}$ with $10$ horizontal divisions for the diagonal scale to read down to $0.01\text{ km}$ ($10\text{ m}$). draw diagonal lines on the first section.

4. **Time Calculation & Marking:**
   - Time taken to cover $4.56\text{ km}$ at $50\text{ km/hr}$:
     $$\text{Time} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Speed}} = \frac{4.56\text{ km}}{50\text{ km/hr}} = 0.0912\text{ hours} = 5.472\text{ minutes} \approx 5\text{ min } 28\text{ sec}$$
   - Mark the distance of $4.56\text{ km}$ on the diagonal scale (4 main divisions, 5 small horizontal units up, and 6th diagonal intersection).
proTip: Always calculate RF clearly and verify the diagonal sub-divisions correspond correctly to the required decimal places.
